summary: Econo-Mix Metering and Mixing System for low to medium viscosity two-component reactive materials. We characterize the ECONO-MIX by its simplicity in function and design, friendliness of operation, and ease of maintenance. This system is a competitive starter model in two-component metering and mixing technology. This system is capable of processing most reactive polymers, like polyurethanes, silicones, and epoxy resins. They can be unfilled, filled as well, or slightly abrasive. The ECONO-MIX unit is a dependable and reliable two-component metering and mixing proportioning system that is best used for small to medium production applications. Customization of the base system is available as necessary for the specific application. The ECONO-MIX is a solvent-free, positive displacement piston pump type metering and mixing system, used to handle low to medium viscosity multi-component media such as epoxy resins, polyurethanes, or silicones with a volumetric mixing ratio of between 1:1 and 6.25:1.

paragraphs: Low-pressure feed systems, such as diaphragm pumps or pressure vessels, are used to supply the material into the positive displacement piston metering pumps. Pressure tanks can be mounted onto the machine chassis, or a remote bulk feed unit is available for feeding directly from 55-gallon drums.

The pumps are driven by a single air motor. A lever system connects the pumps and the drive. The pump for the A component is fixed to the lever system and shares the same stroke length as the drive motor. The pump for the B component is adjustable along a lever system providing a variable stroke length, which is used for the fine adjustment of the mixing ratio.

The ECONO-MIX is typically fitted with our standard two-component static mixing system that includes a twin snuffer valve combined with a disposable static mixer. The valve contains an infinitely adjustable “snuff back” effect to avoid dripping after metering has finished. Should mixed material be allowed to cure in the mixer, it can be replaced simply and inexpensively, thus avoiding a time-consuming, expensive, and environmentally damaging solvent flushing cycle.
Optionally, we can offer both dynamic mixers and/or dynamic static mixer valves where the material requires an aggressive blending cycle necessary to achieve its proper mix.

title: Static Mixer System
tagline: Kirkco's Solventless Static Mixer System
summary: Kirkco's innovative metering and mixing system features a solventless design for components A and B. These components are meticulously fed separately up to the dispense valve, utilizing specialized valve stems and nozzles equipped with check valves. The valve stems are engineered to exert a snuff back effect upon closing, effectively preventing any undesired dripping from the static mixer tube outlet. Notably, the snuff effect is fully adjustable using a convenient knurled screw.

sections.heading: Plastic Static Mixer
paragraphs: The system incorporates a plastic static mixer designed for the homogeneous blending of two-component materials. In this process, the materials are individually fed until they converge at the inlet edge of the mixer. The mixer's helical spirals within the mix tube play a crucial role, continuously dividing the material flow and seamlessly blending the two components. The layout of these spirals generates a rotary effect, ensuring a radially homogeneous mix of the components.

Importantly, the two components remain distinct until entering the mixer, guaranteeing that homogeneous mixing occurs precisely at that juncture. The mixed material is then dispensed with a carefully controlled snuff effect upon closure, preventing any residual dripping. This snuffer effect is fully customizable through the use of a user-friendly knurled knob. Remarkably, the entire process is achieved without the need for solvent flushing, emphasizing the system's efficiency and environmental consciousness.

tagline: Volume Counters for Accurate Lubricant Tracking & Flow Verification
summary: A volume counter is a device that tracks the cumulative total volume of fluid moving through a lubrication or fluid delivery system. By capturing totalizer readings based on pulses from a flow meter or gear sensor, a volume counter helps operators verify usage, monitor system performance, and support maintenance planning. In lubrication systems, this means accurate records of grease or oil delivered, whether for quality control, preventive maintenance, or inventory tracking.

sections.heading: Digital Volume Counter
paragraphs: A digital counter that displays the totalized volume of lubricant delivered based on signals from flow monitoring devices. Ideal for systems where accuracy, ease of reading, and data tracking are important.

sections.heading: Key Features:
paragraphs: Digital display with cumulative total reading
Compatible with pulse outputs from flow meters
High-resolution counting for precise records
Reset or non-resettable options per system needs
Easy mounting near application points or operator stations

sections.heading: Benefits:
paragraphs: Clear real-time usage tracking
Supports maintenance planning and documentation
Improves transparency in automated lubrication systems

sections.heading: Ideal For:
paragraphs: Industrial and centralized lubrication networks
Production lines with usage verification requirements
Quality tracking and reporting environments

sections.heading: Mechanical Volume Counter
paragraphs: A rugged, mechanical totalizer designed for harsh environments where simplicity and durability are priorities. Works with compatible flow sensors or gear meters to accumulate volume based on mechanical pulses.

sections.heading: Key Features:
paragraphs: Durable mechanical gearing for robust operation
Analog totalizer dial with high readability
Works with pulse signals from compatible meters
No external power required for basic models

sections.heading: Benefits:
paragraphs: Reliable in environments with electrical limitations
Easy to service and maintain
Clear cumulative usage readout

sections.heading: Ideal For:
paragraphs: Heavy equipment lubrication systems
Remote or non-powered installations
Centralized feed systems where visual verification is preferred
